meta.topic: Change affects multiple applications and teams

problem:
Meridian Bank must change its instant euro payments to match the current scheme rules: there is no longer a scheme-level maximum amount for SCT Inst, execution must complete within 10 seconds, and verification of payee is mandatory for instant euro payments. The change touches the mobile app, the payment engine, the sanctions and fraud services, the clearing adapter, the ledger, the customer notification service, the reconciliation process and the contact centre scripts. Each team sees only its own part, and nobody has yet mapped the full impact.

Without a proper impact analysis, the bank could release a change that lets a large payment through without a limit check, or that fails verification of payee for a valid beneficiary, or that breaks a downstream consumer that still expects the old maximum. The learner must trace the change upstream and downstream across systems, data, interfaces, controls, tests, operations and release dependencies, and produce a plan that every team can work from.
solution:
Build the impact analysis as a map, not as a list of opinions. Start from the change and walk upstream: which channels, products and customer journeys can submit an instant euro payment, which limits and validations apply today, and which of those must change? Then walk downstream: the payment engine, fraud and sanctions checks, verification of payee, routing, the clearing adapter, the ledger, notifications, reconciliation and reporting. For each system, record what changes, what stays the same, and what breaks if the change is made without it.

Cover data and interfaces explicitly. The removal of the scheme maximum does not mean the bank has no limits: bank-level limits, customer limits and fraud thresholds still apply and must be reviewed. Verification of payee adds a new check with its own data, timing and failure handling, and its result must be recorded against the payment. Any interface that carried the old maximum, or that assumed a maximum existed, must be found through a consumer inventory, and breaking changes must be versioned with a deprecation period and contract tests.

Cover controls, tests, operations and release. Map the dependencies between checks: independent checks can run in parallel to protect the 10-second execution limit, while checks that depend on another result must stay sequential. Define the timeout budget for each check and the fail-open or fail-closed policy. Plan tests end to end, not per system, including a large-value payment, a verification of payee mismatch, a timeout in one check, and a downstream consumer still on the old version. Plan the release order, the rollback for each step, the operational staffing, the reconciliation checks after go-live, and the customer communication. No team builds until the map, the sequencing and the rollback are agreed.

decision.question: Meridian Bank must remove the SCT Inst scheme maximum, meet the 10-second execution limit, and make verification of payee mandatory. The change touches many applications and teams. What is the best first step?

options.label: A
options.detail: Ask each team to make its own change and coordinate at go-live.

options.label: B
options.detail: Release the change to one channel and see what breaks.

options.label: C
options.detail: Trace the change upstream and downstream across systems, data, interfaces, controls, tests, operations and release dependencies, and agree the sequencing, the versioning and the rollback plan before any team builds.

options.label: D
options.detail: Change the payment engine only, since that is where the limit lives.

decisionRationale: Option C is correct because a change that crosses many systems can only be delivered safely when its full impact is mapped and its sequencing and rollback are agreed first. Option A leaves integration to chance. Option D ignores the channel, screening, ledger and reconciliation impacts. Option B uses production customers as the test.

steps.title: Documents the scheme change and its business intent
Traces the change upstream to channels, products and customer journeys
Traces the change downstream through engine, screening, verification of payee, clearing, ledger and reconciliation
Maps data and interface impacts, consumer inventory and versioning needs
Agrees sequencing, timeout budgets, parallel and sequential controls, and the rollback plan
Runs end-to-end tests for large values, verification mismatches, timeouts and old-version consumers
Prepares staffing, monitoring, reconciliation checks and customer communication
Releases in the agreed order, verifies each step, and rolls back if a check fails

happy: The impact map is agreed, every consumer of the old maximum is found and migrated, verification of payee is built with clear failure handling, and end-to-end tests pass for large values, mismatches and timeouts. The release runs in order, reconciliation confirms the first day of live payments, and customers experience faster, verified instant payments with no broken channel.

negative.title: Unknown downstream consumer
negative.detail: A consumer still expects the old maximum and rejects large payments. Maintain a consumer inventory and contract tests. Version the change, keep the old behaviour during an agreed deprecation period, and assess impact before release.

negative.title: One control times out
negative.detail: A screening or verification check exceeds its budget and the 10-second execution limit is at risk. Define timeout budgets and a fail-open or fail-closed policy per check. Run independent checks in parallel and keep dependent checks sequential.

negative.title: Late negative result after release
negative.detail: A check returns a negative result after the payment has already been released. Never release before all mandatory decisions are recorded. Define the aggregation rule and the handling for late results in the design.

negative.title: Character encoding changes a name
negative.detail: A beneficiary name contains characters a downstream rail or legacy interface does not support. Apply documented character-set rules and transliteration only where permitted, preserve the original value, and record the transformation.

technical: Keep a consumer inventory and a schema registry so every consumer of every changed field is known. Use explicit versioning, prefer additive evolution, and run contract tests on every release. Map the dependency graph between controls: independent checks run in parallel, dependent checks stay sequential, and the release waits for all mandatory decisions. Define timeout budgets that fit inside the 10-second execution limit, with a fail-open or fail-closed policy per check. Record the verification of payee result, the limit applied and the decision for every payment, with correlation IDs across all systems. Preserve the original beneficiary name alongside any transformed value, and apply documented character-set rules only. Log every decision with its timestamp for audit.

accounting: Removing the scheme maximum does not remove bank-level or customer-level limits, and those limits must be reviewed and recorded before go-live. Large-value instant payments need liquidity and settlement monitoring, and operations must be able to see them on a worklist with an owner. Verification of payee mismatches go to a controlled exception queue with a service level, never to an automatic release or an automatic rejection without a defined rule. Reconciliation after go-live must confirm that payments, ledger postings and clearing reports agree for the new flow, including large values. Any rollback must return each system to a consistent state, with no payment left half-released.

questions.question: What is the SCT Inst scheme maximum now?
options: There is no scheme-level maximum now; the EUR 100,000 cap was removed.
questions.explanation: The EPC SCT Inst Rulebook 2025 removed the EUR 100,000 scheme maximum. Bank-level and customer-level limits still apply.

questions.question: What is the maximum execution time for an instant euro payment?
questions.explanation: Regulation (EU) 2024/886 sets maximum execution at 10 seconds, with sub-timelines of 5, 7 and 9 seconds.

questions.question: Which checks can safely run in parallel?
options: Independent checks whose results do not depend on each other; dependent checks must stay sequential.
None, all checks must be sequential.
questions.explanation: Parallel execution is safe only where no check needs another check result or enrichment first.

questions.question: A downstream consumer still expects the old maximum. How is it handled?
options: Find it through the consumer inventory, version the change, run contract tests, and agree migration before release.
Change the consumer without telling it.
questions.explanation: A consumer inventory and versioning protect unknown or unready consumers from a breaking change.
